title: The Brethren Ask
summary: After Nephi reads from the plates of brass, his brethren come to him and ask what the things he read mean.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi had read things engraven upon the plates of brass.
Afterward, Nephi's brethren came to him and asked what the things he read meant.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi and his brethren are together when they speak.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether the plates are present or nearby.
The appearance and age of Nephi's brethren.
The plates' material appearance and the surroundings.

spoken_dialogue.text: What meaneth these things which ye have read?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi's brethren

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, are they to be understood according to things which are spiritual, which shall come to pass according to the spirit and not the flesh?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi's brethren

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the visions or events in the plates as occurring in this scene.
Do not depict the plates as present or nearby; the verse does not specify their location when the brethren come to Nephi.

title: The Spirit Makes Things Known
summary: Nephi answers that the things were manifested to the prophet by the voice of the Spirit.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says the things were manifested to the prophet by the voice of the Spirit.
Nephi says all things that shall come upon humanity according to the flesh are made known to prophets by the Spirit.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi speaks to his brethren in the same conversation.
unspecified_visual_details: Which prophet is meant and what the Spirit's voice looked or sounded like.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold they were manifest unto the prophet by the voice of the Spirit;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Spirit's voice is reported as an explanation, not narrated as a visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Spirit as a visible figure.

title: Scattered Among the Nations
summary: Nephi explains that the house of Israel will be scattered among nations, and that many tribes have already been led away and scattered across the isles of the sea.

explicit_facts.text: The things Nephi read pertain to temporal and spiritual matters.
The house of Israel will be scattered over the earth and among all nations.
Many are already lost from the knowledge of those at Jerusalem; most tribes have been led away and scattered to the isles of the sea, and their whereabouts are unknown.
Nephi says those led away, and those later scattered and confounded because of the Holy One of Israel, will be scattered among nations and hated by all men.

unspecified_visual_details: The people, places, and periods represented by the scattering.

narration.text: the house of Israel, sooner or later, will be scattered upon all the face of the earth,
the more part of all the tribes have been led away;
they shall be scattered among all nations and shall be hated of all men.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi's account is explanatory speech; no scattering event is narrated as happening in the present scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage a specific historical scattering as a present event.

title: Nursed by the Gentiles
summary: Nephi explains that the Gentiles will nurse the scattered people, while the Lord lifts up his hand upon the Gentiles and sets them up as a standard.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says the people will be nursed by the Gentiles.
The Lord has lifted up his hand upon the Gentiles and set them up for a standard.
Their children are carried in arms and their daughters upon shoulders.
Nephi says these are temporal things, concerning the covenants with their fathers, Nephi's people in days to come, and their brethren of the house of Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Children being held in arms or carried on shoulders may illustrate the language of the passage.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity, clothing, setting, and historical period of the people described.

narration.text: after they shall be nursed by the Gentiles,
their children have been carried in their arms,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The nursing and carrying language describes the prophecy; avoid presenting it as a separately dated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent identifiable Gentile or Israelite individuals.

title: A Mighty Nation and a Marvelous Work
summary: Nephi says the Lord will raise up a mighty nation among the Gentiles on this land, by whom their seed will be scattered, and afterward do a marvelous work among the Gentiles for their seed's benefit.

explicit_facts.text: After Israel is scattered and confounded, the Lord God will raise a mighty nation among the Gentiles upon this land, and by them Nephi's seed will be scattered.
After their seed is scattered, the Lord God will do a marvelous work among the Gentiles of great worth to their seed, likened to being nourished and carried.

unspecified_visual_details: The nation, land, and marvelous work's visual form.

narration.text: the Lord God will raise up a mighty nation among the Gentiles,
the Lord God will proceed to do a marvelous work among the Gentiles,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The marvelous work and nursing comparison are explained in prophecy, not shown as a separate present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the nation, its founders, or a visual form for the marvelous work.

title: Blessings to All Kindreds
summary: Nephi teaches that the covenants and gospel will be made known to Israel, and that all kindreds of the earth can be blessed through the Lord's work among the nations.

explicit_facts.text: The work will benefit the Gentiles and all the house of Israel by making known the Father's covenants with Abraham.
Nephi says all kindreds of the earth cannot be blessed unless the Lord makes bare his arm in the eyes of the nations.
The Lord God will make bare his arm among all nations in bringing covenants and the gospel to the house of Israel.

unspecified_visual_details: The visual form of the figurative phrase “make bare his arm.”

narration.text: In thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.
the Lord God will proceed to make bare his arm in the eyes of all the nations,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Make bare his arm” is figurative language; do not depict a literal divine arm.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a divine figure or literal arm not described as visibly appearing.

title: Brought Out of Captivity
summary: Nephi says the Lord will bring Israel out of captivity and gather them to their lands of inheritance, out of obscurity and darkness.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord will bring Israel out of captivity and gather them to their lands of inheritance.
They will be brought out of obscurity and darkness and know the Lord as Savior, Redeemer, and Mighty One of Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Movement from darkness into light may suggest the figurative contrast, without depicting it as a supernatural event.
unspecified_visual_details: The captivity, lands of inheritance, and manner of gathering.

narration.text: he will bring them again out of captivity,
they shall know that the Lord is their Savior and their Redeemer,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The gathering is prophetic description, not a present event in Nephi's conversation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray a specific captivity or claim a particular historical fulfillment.

title: Those Who War Against Israel
summary: Nephi prophesies that those who war against Israel will turn against one another and fall by their own actions, and that the great and abominable church will fall.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says the blood of the great and abominable church will turn upon its own heads and its members will war among themselves.
Nations warring against Israel will turn against one another and fall into the pit they dug to ensnare the Lord's people.
Those who fight against Zion will be destroyed, and the great and abominable church will tumble to the dust.

unspecified_visual_details: The church's visual representation, the nations, and the conflicts' setting.

narration.text: they shall war among themselves,
they shall fall into the pit which they digged to ensnare the people of the Lord.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The pit and the church tumbling to dust may be figurative; no specific battle is narrated here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict gore, specific combatants, or a literal church building collapsing.

title: The Proud as Stubble
summary: Nephi prophesies that the proud and wicked will be burned, while the Lord preserves the righteous and they need not fear.

explicit_facts.text: The time will come when Satan has no more power over human hearts, and the proud and wicked will be as stubble and burned.
The fulness of God's wrath will be poured out upon humanity, but he will not allow the wicked to destroy the righteous.
The Lord will preserve the righteous by his power, even through the destruction of their enemies by fire; the righteous need not fear.

unspecified_visual_details: The prophetic fire's setting, scale, and visible subjects.

narration.text: all the proud and they who do wickedly shall be as stubble;
the righteous need not fear;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “As stubble” is a comparison; do not depict people literally as stubble.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict gore or invent a specific fire event or its victims.

title: Blood, Fire, and Smoke
summary: Nephi says blood, fire, and vapor of smoke must come upon the earth if people harden their hearts against the Holy One of Israel, and that the righteous will not perish.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says blood, fire, and vapor of smoke must come upon the earth if people harden their hearts against the Holy One of Israel.
The righteous shall not perish, and those who fight against Zion will be cut off.

unspecified_visual_details: The event, its time, its participants, and how the imagery appears.

narration.text: blood, and fire, and vapor of smoke must come;
the righteous shall not perish;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophecy, not a narrated present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a disaster scene or show blood or injury.

title: The Prophet Moses Spoke Of
summary: Nephi recalls Moses's words about a prophet whom the people must hear, then identifies that prophet as the Holy One of Israel, who will execute judgment in righteousness.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord will prepare a way for his people, fulfilling Moses's words that the Lord will raise a prophet like Moses whom the people must hear.
Those who will not hear that prophet will be cut off from among the people.
Nephi identifies the prophet as the Holy One of Israel, who will execute judgment in righteousness.

unspecified_visual_details: The prophet's appearance and the scene of judgment.

narration.text: A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you, like unto me;
this prophet of whom Moses spake was the Holy One of Israel;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moses is mentioned in quoted teaching but is not present in the scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moses or the Holy One of Israel visibly; no appearance is described here.

title: The Kingdom of the Devil
summary: Nephi contrasts the righteous, who need not fear, with the kingdom of the devil and those who seek gain, power, popularity, worldly things, and iniquity; these will be brought low and consumed as stubble.

explicit_facts.text: The righteous need not fear and will not be confounded.
The kingdom of the devil is established among people in the flesh.
Nephi says churches built for gain, power, popularity, or worldly lusts and iniquity belong to that kingdom and must be brought low and consumed as stubble.

unspecified_visual_details: The visual appearance of the kingdom or the churches described.

narration.text: the righteous need not fear,
all those who belong to the kingdom of the devil are they who need fear,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The kingdom and stubble language is teaching and metaphor, not a literal supernatural scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Satan, a devil kingdom, or invented church members as visible.

title: The Shepherd and His Fold
summary: Nephi prophesies that the righteous will be led up as calves of the stall, the Holy One of Israel will reign, and he will gather his children as one fold under one shepherd.

explicit_facts.text: The righteous must be led up as calves of the stall, and the Holy One of Israel must reign in dominion, might, power, and glory.
He gathers his children from the four quarters of the earth, numbers his sheep, and they know him; there will be one fold and one shepherd, who feeds his sheep.

unspecified_visual_details: Whether the sheep and fold are literal or figurative, and the Holy One's appearance.

narration.text: there shall be one fold and one shepherd;
he shall feed his sheep,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The flock and shepherd language is figurative teaching; do not invent a visible appearance for the Holy One.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Holy One of Israel as a visible figure.

title: Righteousness and Peace
summary: Nephi explains that Satan will have no power over a righteous people, and that all nations and peoples may dwell safely in the Holy One of Israel if they repent.

explicit_facts.text: Because of his people's righteousness, Satan has no power over their hearts and cannot be loosed for many years; the Holy One of Israel reigns.
Nephi says these things must come according to the flesh.
All nations, kindreds, tongues, and people may dwell safely in the Holy One of Israel if they repent.

unspecified_visual_details: The people, place, and visual form of dwelling safely.

narration.text: they dwell in righteousness,
all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people shall dwell safely in the Holy One of Israel

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Satan is referred to in teaching but is not described as visibly present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Satan or the Holy One of Israel as visible.

title: Nephi Makes an End
summary: Nephi says he will not speak further about these things yet, urges his brethren to consider the truth of the plates of brass and the need for obedience, and concludes that obedience and endurance bring salvation at the last day.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi makes an end and says he dares not speak further yet concerning these things.
Nephi urges his brethren to consider that the things written on the plates of brass are true and testify that people must obey God's commandments.
Nephi says he and his father are not the only ones who have testified and taught these things; those obedient to the commandments and enduring to the end will be saved at the last day.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi concludes speaking to his brethren.
unspecified_visual_details: The brethren's reactions and the setting's appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: Wherefore, my brethren, I would that ye should consider that the things which have been written upon the plates of brass are true;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: ye shall be saved at the last day.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

prohibited_inventions: Do not add a response from Nephi's brethren.
